issues.explanation: For trauma to a loved one, bus riding is not impossible but is hard to justify here because the rest of the profile provides no transport-related memory or appraisal content linking the trauma to buses or commuting. With Triggers strongly tied to Negative Appraisals in the formulation, the trigger set should plausibly connect to the appraisal themes; this item appears isolated.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted
issues.explanation: Self-blame can occur after trauma to a loved one, but in this profile it implies perceived causal responsibility for the loved one's trauma. That responsibility theme is not supported by the memory items, which are mainly sensory re-experiencing, nor by the other trigger content. The appraisal therefore feels insufficiently grounded in the rest of the selected profile.

For trauma to a loved one, 'Entrapment: Having no options' is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which centers on victim-focused reminders and guilt about failing to protect others rather than a personal entrapment situation. It implies a different trauma context unless more detail is provided.

issues.item: Memory: Taste Vividness: I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns
issues.explanation: 'Taste Vividness' is difficult to fit with the selected trauma type and the rest of the memory profile. In a loved-one trauma profile with auditory and narrative-fragmentation features, gustatory reliving is possible but here feels disconnected and unusually specific without any other sensory context supporting why taste would be central.

vignette: John, a 55-year-old man of Oceania ethnicity, has spent most of his life in service roles, currently working as a nanny for a family with young children. His history is marked by significant trauma stemming from an event where he was unable to protect a loved one. John's experience has left him with deep-seated emotional and psychological scars that have progressively affected various aspects of his daily life. The traumatic event occurred several years ago when John was caring for his ex-wife's sister, who was in critical condition due to a sudden illness. During this time, he was responsible for her round-the-clock care, which included helping her with basic tasks and ensuring she received proper medical attention. Despite his best efforts, the situation took a tragic turn one night when his ex-wife's sister passed away unexpectedly while John was by her side. Since then, John has struggled to make sense of what happened and feels an overwhelming sense of guilt and weakness for not being able to prevent her death. When he tries to explain the event to others, he often loses the thread of his story, becoming emotionally overwhelmed and unable to finish. These gaps in his memory are compounded by auditory recall - moments when he hears specific sounds that were present during the traumatic night, such as the beeping of medical equipment or the last words spoken. John's sense of self has been deeply affected by these experiences. He often feels like an object rather than a person and believes he is weak for not being able to protect his loved one. These negative appraisals significantly impact how he remembers the event, making it difficult for him to confront the memories without feeling immense grief and self-blame. His triggers are potent reminders of this experience - specific body parts that remind him of his ex-wife's sister, visual cues from news stories about similar tragedies, and conversations about people losing loved ones. Each trigger intensifies his negative appraisals, leading him to feel more dehumanized and weak, which in turn deepens the emotional turmoil he experiences when recalling the event. John's occupation as a nanny places him in an environment where these triggers are particularly poignant. The sound of a child crying or seeing children with medical conditions can trigger memories that flood his mind with grief and self-doubt. As a result, John has started to avoid certain tasks and situations at work, which has led to increased tension with the family he works for. He has come to believe that his failures extend beyond just this one incident, reinforcing his sense of inadequacy. The loop of negative appraisals leading to memory disturbances and heightened triggers creates a cycle that tightens over time. John finds himself increasingly isolated, both at work and in his personal life, as he withdraws from situations that might provoke these memories and feelings of weakness. His relationships have suffered, particularly with the family he works for, where his avoidance behaviors have been noticed but not fully understood. What finally brought John to seek help was a culmination of these cumulative effects - feeling increasingly isolated, struggling with his work responsibilities due to his emotional state, and fearing that he might never be able to break free from this cycle of guilt and grief. He is most afraid of continuing to feel weak and dehumanized but also hopes for the possibility of finding peace with his past and regaining a sense of self-worth. In therapy, John aims to address these interconnected issues - breaking the cycle where negative appraisals lead to memory disturbances and heightened triggers, which in turn reinforce his negative beliefs. He seeks to regain control over his life and find meaning beyond the shadows cast by this traumatic event.
